When you're choosing a medical record retrieval service for a plaintiff firm, the decision usually comes down to completeness, accuracy, and how much time your team spends chasing providers. Retrieval timing varies by provider, request scope, authorization requirements, and vendor, and gaps found late in a case can be costly. This guide looks at the top alternatives for personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice firms, and at why[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) stands out by pairing retrieval and missing record checks with human-verified AI insights, with advertised turnaround of a couple of weeks rather than months.

-


Codes Health stands out as a leading alternative, combining retrieval, Missing Record Review, potential breach-of-care flags, and AI-generated insights verified by humans, with advertised turnaround of a couple of weeks, not months


-


Codes Health's position is that services promising same-day retrieval often return only the records immediately available, which requires added client involvement to fill the gaps and can contribute to churn. Ask whether a turnaround figure measures initial delivery, individual provider responses, or completion of all requested records


-


Human review adds a quality-control step on top of AI speed, though attorneys should still verify material findings against source records


-

-


Litigation-focused features, including potential breach-of-care flags, future medical expense information, and pre-existing condition identification, support attorney review in plaintiff cases


-

-


General AI platforms like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review, and AI-generated analysis can contain errors or omissions


## **What RecordX Offers and Why Firms Compare Alternatives**


RecordX, offered by CatalyzeX, advertises AI-assisted retrieval workflows supported by human specialists, daily provider follow-up, activity tracking, and a reported 14 to 30 day turnaround. Firms comparing it with other options usually look at a few specific differences: how each service checks for missing records, what analysis comes with retrieval, how pricing is structured, and how well it connects with existing case management systems.


### **Common Retrieval Challenges Firms Want Solved**


-


Timelines that vary widely by provider and request scope


-


Incomplete records that require follow-up requests


-


Missing documentation discovered during trial preparation


-


Authorization errors that cause provider rejections and delays


-


Analysis that's sold separately or not offered at all; capabilities and fees vary by provider, and some retrieval services also offer summaries, chronologies, and review


-


Per-page pricing that creates budget surprises on large records


### **What Plaintiff Firms Look For**


Personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice cases depend on complete medical documentation. Missing treatment records can undermine damages arguments and give opposing counsel unexpected openings. A strong alternative combines retrieval with useful analysis, proactive gap detection, and predictable pricing.

Authorization pre-checks matter more than they might seem. Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can force a resubmission and put a request back at the start of the provider's response window. Under the[30-day federal standard](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/how-timely-must-a-covered-entity-be/index.html) for HIPAA access requests, providers generally have 30 calendar days to act, and state timelines vary. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


For high-volume customers, Codes Health builds custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software, subject to technical scope and feasibility. Through its[Filevine partnership](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/filevine-partners-with-codes-health-to-bring-ai-native-medical-record-retrieval-to-legal-teams-302823827.html) announced on July 13, 2026, Filevine users can initiate requests, track progress, and receive completed records without leaving their case file.

## **Comparing Retrieval Speed and Completeness**


Turnaround figures aren't always measured the same way. One vendor's number may reflect initial delivery, another's an average across individual provider responses, and another's completion of every requested record.


Codes Health's position is that services promising same-day retrieval often return only the records immediately available, which requires added client involvement to track down the rest and can contribute to client churn. Whatever service you choose, ask how it defines a completed retrieval.


Codes Health focuses on completeness through Missing Record Review, which cross-references patient history before records reach your legal team. Missing treatment documentation discovered during trial preparation can undermine damages arguments, give opposing counsel unexpected openings, delay settlement negotiations, and weaken expert testimony. Catching missing facilities, date ranges, and billing records before the file closes helps firms avoid those problems.


## **Why General AI Platforms Fall Short**


General-purpose AI tools like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review. AI-generated medical record analysis can contain errors or omissions, so attorneys should verify material findings against source records and evaluate each tool's confidentiality safeguards and suitability, consistent with[ABA ethics guidance](https://www.americanbar.org/news/abanews/aba-news-archives/2024/07/aba-issues-first-ethics-guidance-ai-tools/) on AI use.


[Codes Health's AI platform](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) is built to analyze medical records with high precision for plaintiff firms:


-


**Litigation-focused outputs:** potential breach-of-care flags, future expense information, and pre-existing condition identification for attorney review


-


**Human verification:** AI-generated insights verified by humans as an added quality-control step


-


**Data handling:** Codes Health states that client data is not used to train its models

What prevents those failures is checking requests before submission, following up until providers respond, and confirming completeness before the file closes.
